name: Network Acquisition-Effect Evidence

positioning.oneLineSummary: Tests whether existing network participation causes efficient new-user acquisition rather than merely correlating with viral or paid growth.
positioning.productLabel: Acquisition-Effect Lens — based on Andrew Chen's public Cold Start materials

attribution.display: Based on Andrew Chen's public Cold Start materials

neutralParaphrase: Measure how existing network nodes expose, invite, or transact with prospective participants and whether that loop creates activated, retained users at improving marginal cost. Keep viral acquisition separate from the value effect that makes the network useful.

locator.value: Organic growth, virality distinction, and atomic-unit measurement

requiredConditions: Acquisition source, activation, and retention can be traced.
Network-mediated and non-network acquisition are separable.

requiredEvidence.description: Existing-node action, prospective-node exposure, conversion, activation, and repeat loop.
Paid, organic, viral, sales, reactivation, churn, CAC, and retained-user economics.
Acquisition efficiency by atomic-network density and stage.

decisionQuestions: Which existing-node behavior creates a new participant?
Does the acquired participant activate and retain?
Does marginal acquisition improve as relevant density rises?
Could the same loop exist without increasing network value?
positiveSignals: A repeatable node-mediated loop produces retained participants.
Organic or viral share rises within maturing atomic networks.
CAC or payback improves without hidden subsidy.
The loop reinforces the core interaction rather than vanity sharing.
redFlags: Referral signups are counted without activation or retention.
Paid acquisition is relabeled network growth.
A viral feature has no user-value dependency.
Global organic growth hides local cold starts.
disconfirmingEvidence: Referral cohorts retain worse than paid cohorts.
Acquisition efficiency does not vary with network density.
Invites are incentive-driven and stop when rewards end.
Most growth comes from a non-network distribution channel.
contraindications: Do not infer network effect from K-factor alone.
Do not count unactivated invites as nodes.
Do not merge acquisition and engagement evidence.

instructions: Map each acquisition loop from existing to retained new node.
Compare efficiency by density and cohort.
Conclude demonstrated, emerging, viral-only, or unsupported.

deterministicRule.prohibition: The language model must not calculate acquisition metrics.

sourceReliability.medium: Event and cohort data support loops.
sourceReliability.high: Auditable graph, spend, activation, retention, and density data converge.

evidenceStrength.medium: Retained organic acquisition exists but density causality is unclear.
evidenceStrength.high: Node-mediated loop and improving density economics are evidenced.

evidenceCoverage.medium: Source, activation, retention covered; cost or local unit partial.
evidenceCoverage.high: Loop, source, activation, retention, CAC, subsidy, density, and counterchannel complete.

applicabilityConfidence.high: Acquisition effect is material to growth.

empiricalQualifications: Acquisition loops depend on host platforms and incentives.

rights.notes: Public doctrine and affiliated metrics are neutrally paraphrased.

openIssues: Define retained-node windows by network archetype.
